**Finding submitted: deviation (§ 7.2, p0027).**

- **What it says:** § 7.2 requires *Customer* to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms we offer any other technology supplier — the MFN runs against us, not in our favour.
- **Why it fails:** No product limitation, no time limit, no comparison carve-outs. That is the rule's walk-away position, not the fallback (defined product / 12 months / reasonable-comparison carve-outs).
- **Internal conflict:** § 12.3 has Vendor acknowledge that we have made "no exclusivity, non-compete, most-favoured-customer, minimum-volume, or no-hire commitment," which § 7.2 contradicts.
- **Redline (validated, preferred level, per precedent seed-mfn):** delete § 7.2 in full. No Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to us is affected.
